items.title: NY DFS Overhauls Independent Dispute Resolution Process with New Guidance and Draft Rules - ACA International
items.reason: New York Department of Financial Services issued guidance and draft rules overhauling the IDR process, which is a core component of No Surprises Act implementation that directly affects revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: New York's Department of Financial Services (DFS) has released new guidance and draft rules restructuring the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process under the No Surprises Act. This state-level rulemaking activity affects how healthcare providers and insurers resolve out-of-network billing disputes in New York, a key revenue-cycle function. The overhaul likely establishes new procedural requirements, timelines, or documentation standards for IDR submissions and determinations. Revenue-cycle teams in New York will need to update their dispute-resolution workflows and compliance procedures to align with the DFS's new expectations, making this material to operational planning and dispute management strategies.

items.title: Investor suit says UnitedHealth ignored governance, cybersecurity gaps for years
items.reason: This is a shareholder litigation suit against UnitedHealth (a major payer) alleging governance failures and cybersecurity neglect related to operational practices, which falls within payer litigation and enforcement actions.
items.summary: Two shareholder groups filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth alleging the company misled investors by ignoring governance and cybersecurity gaps for years, including shuttering an internal Medicare billing audit function and failing to address security lapses that contributed to the Change Healthcare cyberattack. The suit targets UnitedHealth's board and management for breach of fiduciary duty in governance oversight. This litigation is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because it highlights potential vulnerabilities in major payer operations and governance practices that can disrupt claims processing and billing systems, as demonstrated by the Change Healthcare breach's impact on provider operations.
